title.justification: The title 'Reward is enough' is directly mentioned at the beginning of the document as the main hypothesis being explored.
title.quote: In this article we hypothesise that intelligence, and its associated abilities, can be understood as subserving the maximisation of reward.

analysis.description: The paper presents the hypothesis that maximizing reward is sufficient to drive intelligent behavior, potentially leading to artificial general intelligence. It discusses how various abilities associated with intelligence, such as perception, language, and social intelligence, can emerge from the maximization of reward signals in complex environments.

type.justification: The paper primarily presents a theoretical hypothesis about intelligence and its relation to reward maximization, rather than conducting empirical experiments.
type.quote: In this article we hypothesise that intelligence, and its associated abilities, can be understood as subserving the maximisation of reward.

name.justification: The paper discusses the maximization of reward, a core concept within reinforcement learning, and explores its implications for intelligence.
name.quote: We have seen, in the previous section, that rewards are sufficient to express a wide variety of goals, corresponding to the diverse purposes towards which intelligence may be directed.

name.justification: The paper explores the potential for reward maximization to lead to artificial general intelligence.
name.quote: ...powerful reinforcement learning agents could constitute a solution to artificial general intelligence.

name.justification: The paper considers how maximizing reward can lead to social intelligence in agents.
name.quote: Social intelligence is the ability to understand and interact effectively with other agents.

name.justification: AlphaZero is discussed in the context of reinforcement learning and reward maximization as a means to achieve a variety of abilities in games like Go, Chess, and Shogi.
name.quote: AlphaZero focused instead on a singular goal: maximising a reward signal that is 0 until the final step, and then + 1 for winning or − 1 for losing. This ultimately resulted in a deeper understanding of each ability...

is_contributed.justification: The paper references AlphaZero as an existing model, not a contribution of this research.
is_contributed.quote: A recent salutary example of both problem and solution based on reward maximisation comes from the game of Go... AlphaZero...

is_executed.justification: AlphaZero's implementation involves practical execution which is heavily reliant on computational processes typically utilizing GPUs, especially given its application in complex games.
is_executed.quote: ...applying the same method to different environments such as chess or shogi resulted in new abilities such as piece mobility and colour complexes.

is_compared.justification: AlphaZero is compared to other models and approaches in the context of its achievements in board games like Chess and Go.
is_compared.quote: AlphaZero learned (see Section 1) an integrated intelligence across many facets of Go...

referenced_paper_title.value: Mastering the game of go without human knowledge
referenced_paper_title.justification: The referenced paper on AlphaZero is mentioned in the context of its contributions to reinforcement learning and game strategies.
referenced_paper_title.quote: ...AlphaZero learned (see Section 1) an integrated intelligence across many facets of Go.
